loops.minute_1: Player clicks cookie, gains 1 cookie. Golden Cookies spawn randomly (every ~4-8 min), granting 7x multiplier or lump-sum bonus. Immediate sensory feedback (click sound, floating text) drives continued interaction within first 30-60 sec window before first building purchase.
loops.minute_10: Player buys first buildings (Cursor: 15 cookies, Grandma: 100 cookies, Farm: 1100 cookies). Shifts from active clicking to passive production monitoring (cookies/second). Economic tension emerges: exponential cost vs. linear cookie income. Decision point: breadth (many cheap buildings) vs. depth (single expensive high-output building).
loops.hour_5: Player engages minigames (Garden, Stock Market) and interacts with Wrinklers (passive production reducers that accumulate interest, popped on Golden Cookie for 10-100x return). Prestige calculation visible: 1 trillion cookies baked all-time = 1 Prestige Level = +1% CPS permanent. Establishes daily-session pattern (leave Wrinklers overnight, pop combo in morning for massive gain).
loops.endgame: Ascension cycle dominates. Player resets progress (~99.9% cookies, buildings, upgrades gone) but retains Prestige Levels and Heavenly Chips (spent on permanent upgrades). Each ascension grants steeper start for next run. Sugar Lumps (slow-accumulating resources) level buildings for 2x+ efficiency. 600+ achievements provide infinite collect goals. No win state or loss state; endgame = player-defined milestones (reach 10^50 cookies, unlock all achievements, max Prestige).

objectives.player_goal: Accumulate cookies exponentially via purchasing buildings and upgrades; maximize Prestige Levels through ascending cycles; unlock 600+ achievements; customize Heavenly Chip spending for optimal cookie production chains.

games.retention_answer: Cookie Clicker retains players through five reinforcement mechanisms: (1) Exponential growth providing constant numerical momentum and sense of progress; (2) Golden Cookie spawns creating random-interval rewards (slot-machine effect) driving check-in frequency; (3) Achievement system providing 600+ parallel progression paths (collection, numerical, exploit); (4) Ascension resets justifying repeated playthroughs with cumulative bonuses (players ascend 5-10 times over 100h); (5) Minigame variety (Garden, Stock Market) preventing mechanic fatigue. Players return for daily Wrinkler combo (10-100x multiplier) and periodic new features (seasonal events, new buildings). The prestige system is critical: without reset cycles, exponential progression plateaus into boredom (~48h plateau). With cycles, endless replayability emerges.

loops.minute_1: Player places food (tuna, sakura meal) and toys (cushion, cardboard box) in yard, then closes app (mandatory 30+ sec absence). Returns to find a cat visiting (e.g., Tabby). Miaow sound, gentle animation. Player photographs for Catbook. Feedback is purely visual/aesthetic (cute graphics, zero UI clutter). Each placement is creative act, not economic calculation.
loops.minute_10: Player accumulates first fish (currency, left by visiting cats; rate ~1-50 fish per visit, 30 min+ delay before cat leaves). Buys 3-5 additional items (Yarn Ball, Heater) and rearranges yard. New cats attract (some prefer specific toys). Catbook updates. This loop emphasizes design iteration and discovery, not resource optimization. Zero challenge; zero failure states.
loops.hour_5: Player collects enough fish (~500-2000) to purchase rare items (Deluxe variants). Unlocks new cat species (rarer variants). Catbook progress visible (40/100 cats found). Engagement parallels: community activity (forums discuss rare cats, share layouts). This phase is self-paced; can last 20-100h depending on engagement intensity. No time gates; purely voluntary progression.
loops.endgame: Player completes Catbook (100-150 cat variants across all versions). Unlocks rarest cats (gold variants, special editions). Endgame loop shifts from collection to perpetual redecoration: new themes, new yard layouts, expressing aesthetic identity. Neko Atsume 2 (October 2024) resets collection ceiling (50+ new cats, HD graphics, Cat Club subscription option) but preserves core non-competitive aesthetic.

objectives.player_goal: Collect all cat variants (100-150 species); fill Catbook; discover rare cats (gold variants); express creative identity via yard customization; engage with community (share screenshots, discuss rare cat tactics).

games.retention_answer: Neko Atsume retains players through three MDA pillars: (1) Discovery (collectathon): even after 200h, 3-5 undiscovered cats remain, creating permanent 'check back tomorrow' incentive. Rarity is not time-gated or purchasable; it's combinatorial (Tabby only appears near Tuna + Basket). (2) Submission (stress-relief aesthetic): zero timers, zero challenge, zero pressure. Cute graphics, gentle music, fluid animation. Categorized as anti-stress game vs. addictive clickers. Sessions are typically 5-15 min (check yard, feed cats, redesign, quit). (3) Expression (creative systems): yard fully customizable (50+ decors, 20+ themes). Players exhibit their curation to friends/social media. Community sharing drives social retention. No numerical progression (no levels, prestige, or farm-size race); pure aesthetic and collection.
